subject.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting

question: Should the Windows Companion’s default installer deliberately target a prerelease OpenClaw package, or remain on the last released package that completes the supported setup flow until the upstream wizard-runtime correction ships?
rationale: The branch explicitly changes the release contract rather than merely repairing Companion code, and the selected official beta artifact is documented here as failing the core onboarding path.

options.title: Keep a setup-proven default
options.body: Revert the beta default while retaining independently valid Companion fixes, then advance the default only after an official package passes the full supported-path proof.

options.title: Pause for upstream release
options.body: Hold this PR until the separate OpenClaw wizard-runtime correction is released and rerun the current-head WSL setup proof against that exact artifact.

options.title: Accept prerelease default risk
options.body: Approve the beta default only with an explicit maintainer decision that users may encounter the known wizard failure until an upstream release replaces it.

recommendation.title: Keep a setup-proven default
recommendation.body: Revert the beta default while retaining independently valid Companion fixes, then advance the default only after an official package passes the full supported-path proof.

likelyOwner.reason: CassieMei authored the branch’s release-target and setup-path changes and is the clearest available routing candidate for the technical contract.
